items.detail:
Beiyuanmen is the lantern-lit main street everyone photographs, and it is priced and pitched for people who come once. Sajinqiao is the same quarter's other end — 800 m running south from Lianhu Road to Xin Si Lane, no neon, no hawkers — and it is where Xi'an actually eats. Dapiyuan and Xiyangshi sit between the two. Walk west to east and you watch a neighbourhood turn into a theme park.

IT HAS TO BE THE 29th OR THE 30th. The 1st is Golden Week day one and this is the last place you want to be standing in it.
items.dish: Go in at Sajinqiao, not Beiyuanmen

items.detail: Shredded stewed meat chopped on the board and packed into a flatbread fresh out of a clay oven. Pork in the Han shops, beef or lamb in the Hui ones inside the quarter. The bread is the whole thing: it should crackle. Say 我要新鲜的 — wǒ yào xīnxiān de, I want a fresh one — and they will pull one from the oven rather than the pile.

Belt-wide hand-pulled noodles, one noodle to a bowl, under chilli, garlic and a ladle of oil poured over smoking hot at the table so the spices bloom. The character is the most complicated in common use and no keyboard has it, which is why menus print it in pinyin — that is the dish, not a typo.

YOU TEAR THE BREAD YOURSELF. They bring a dense unleavened flatbread and an empty bowl, and the tearing is yours to do: thumbnail-sized pieces, smaller than feels reasonable, which is what lets the lamb broth soak through instead of sliding off. Ten minutes of work before you eat anything. Hand the bowl back and it returns as soup with glass noodles, with pickled garlic and chilli paste on the side.

Lao Sun Jia has been at it since 1898 and is halal; Tong Sheng Xiang is the other hundred-year house.

Cold wheat-starch noodles, slippery and wide, dressed with vinegar, chilli oil, garlic water and cucumber. The thing to order when you have been walking since breakfast and want something that is not hot. Wei Jia is a chain and locals eat at it without embarrassment — there is a branch a few minutes from the Westin.

A thick peppery stew of beef, potato and gluten that Xi'an eats standing up before work, usually with a flatbread torn into it. The window between seven and nine on Sajinqiao is the one time the quarter has no tourists in it at all. Douhua — soft tofu pudding — is the gentler option at the same stalls.

The day the app already keeps clear of anything ticketed. Yuanjia Village Guanzhong Impressions inside Datang Buyecheng does the whole Shaanxi snack repertoire — liangpi, roujiamo, zonggao — under one roof, which is the efficient version of a food street.

CAVEAT: the Tang-themed streets are themselves a holiday magnet after dark. Eat early, or eat in the Joy City mall next door and watch the crowds from a window.

A foreign card on Alipay is free up to ¥200 a transaction and 3% above it, which covers everything here. The trap is smaller: the tiniest stalls show a PERSONAL QR code rather than a merchant one, and a personal code declines a foreign card outright with no useful error. Carry a few hundred in small notes — the same cash you are buying for Tibet, just used earlier.

The ninth lunar month of 2026 begins on 10 OCTOBER — the evening you land. Females carry roe in the ninth month, males fatten in the tenth: 九月圆脐，十月尖, round belly in the ninth, pointed in the tenth. So order female now and don't bother with male until November.

Be honest about where you are in it: this is the first weekend of the season, not its peak, which is the last ten days of October. The crab will be on every menu and it will be real; it will also be better in three weeks, which you do not have. Steamed, with ginger-vinegar and warm yellow wine.

At a good restaurant in season, book.

Jia Jia Tang Bao at No. 127 and Yang's Fry Dumpling at No. 97 face each other across the street, ten minutes from the Metropolo door and five from the Urban Planning Exhibition Centre — which is why this fits the 09:00 slot rather than fighting it. Jia Jia opens at 07:30 and does xiaolongbao and nothing else worth ordering; Yang's opens earlier and does shengjianbao. Have both. ¥30 buys the pair with room to spare.

Get there by eight. By nine the queue at Jia Jia is the point of the photographs.

Not versions of the same thing. XIAOLONGBAO are steamed, the skin near-translucent, and the soup is inside — nibble the top, drink it out, then eat the rest, or you wear it. SHENGJIANBAO are a thicker leavened bun pan-fried to a hard brown bottom, sesame and spring onion on top, and the soup inside them is hotter and comes at you faster. The scald is a genuine rite of passage. Let them sit a minute.

The humblest great dish in the city: noodles, and scallions fried slowly in oil until they collapse, and soy. Four ingredients. A Niang is a proper Shanghainese noodle canteen — yellow croaker noodles, fried pork chop — and it is in the Former French Concession, so it pairs with Tianzifang, which the Sunday plan already lists as the thing that absorbs spare time.

USE THE GROUND-FLOOR TAKEAWAY WINDOW. The 13:45 lunch stop. Two things worth knowing before you join a queue: the ground-floor TAKEAWAY WINDOW and the upstairs dining rooms are different propositions at different prices, and the window moves in minutes where the rooms take an hour. Upstairs is better and you will not have the hour.

It is a tourist institution and priced like one. You will have eaten better dumplings for a third of the money on Huanghe Road at breakfast — which is the argument for doing breakfast properly.

Too late for anything with a reservation and you will have eaten airline food since Lhasa. Huangpu keeps 24-hour noodle and congee shops within a few blocks of Nanjing East Road, and the Haidilao on Nanjing East Road runs all night if you want hotpot at midnight in a city where that is normal.

The convenience stores are the honest answer: a FamilyMart hot counter does tea eggs, braised things and instant noodles with hot water, and one is never more than a block away.

The Sunday timeline has you collecting bags at 18:15 and leaving for Toy Story at 18:45, with 8 km behind you and nothing booked to eat. Two workable answers: eat near the Bund before you go, which costs you nothing because you are already there at sunset; or ride out hungry and eat in Disneytown, which is open late and has the Cheesecake Factory and a food hall. Do not plan on the hotel — Toy Story's own dining is thin and shuts early.
items.dish: Sunday dinner is not in the plan

items.detail:
Gimbap, a rice triangle, banana milk, and back to your seat. The stores run around the clock and take a card.

THE ROOM MATTERS MORE THAN THE FOOD. The same breakfast eaten in the bright 24-hour food court is an hour under fluorescent light at exactly the point Jet lag wants you dim — your target clock says 03:40, the middle of the night. Buy, and go somewhere dark.
items.dish: Convenience store, not the food court

items.detail: Hot Korean breakfast, low light, a seat that reclines, and already paid for through Priority Pass. It is the best room in the terminal for what the jet-lag plan is asking of you, and it solves breakfast and the quiet corner in one move. Tips has the door.

It is the easiest instruction on the page to break while holding a tray at five in the morning, and it is the one that costs the most. Caffeine here buys a comfortable layover and spends your first evening in Xi'an. Jet lag has the reasoning; this is the reminder at the point of temptation.
items.dish: Whatever else you do, no coffee

items.detail:
IT IS ALLOWED, and it is not a loophole. Shanghai Disneyland changed this in 2019 after losing a lawsuit over it, and the rule is now genuinely permissive: outside food and drink are fine as long as nothing needs reheating or refrigerating and nothing smells. No durian, no stinky tofu, no whole watermelons, no instant noodles.

This is the biggest saving available on the leg, and your Snacks row is already tagged Disney. NOT cans or glass, though — see Tips.

The park's flagship and the one that earns 'authentically Disney, distinctly Chinese'. Counter service, not table: wagyu beef noodle soup, Shanghai pork belly rice, proper hot food rather than theme-park food. Several dining rooms, each on its own theme, each hiding a different character — Mushu, Simba, Abu, Chip and Dale, Nemo.

If you eat one sit-down meal inside the park, this is the one.

Quick service ¥40–120. A burger and chips or a rice plate at somewhere like Barbossa's Bounty or Stargazer Grill, drink included, ¥85–115. Table service ¥150–300.

Three days of eating entirely inside the park is roughly ¥600–900. Bringing breakfast and snacks in halves it.

Sunnyside Café does a buffet at ¥178 and it is NOT included in the room. It is also the wrong shape for these mornings: with early entry you are out of the door at 07:00 to walk the 1.5 km, and a buffet is not a thing you do in fifteen minutes.

Buy breakfast the night before in Disneytown or at a convenience store and eat it walking. Save the buffet for a morning you are not queueing for Zootopia.

You walk through it every night anyway, and it stays open past the park. The Cheesecake Factory here is the chain's first Asian flagship; Blue Frog is the reliable ¥101–300 middle. No ticket needed, so it is also where Sunday dinner can land on the way in from the Bund.

And it is where you buy tomorrow's breakfast.
items.where: Between the park and the hotel
